name: Char Siu
desc: Chinese BBQ pork shoulder marinated overnight in hoisin, five spice and garlic, then roasted and basted with a honey glaze.

source.title: Char Siu (Chinese BBQ Pork)
source.evidence: Every ingredient and amount matches the Woks of Life recipe card, and the steps are the same text (475°F dropped to 375°F, 50 minutes total with a rack over water).

ingredients.raw: 3 lb boneless pork shoulder (pork butt), with some good fat on it
ingredients.note: with some good fat on it

ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp Shaoxing rice wine (or dry sherry; optional)
1 1/2 cups water, for the pan, plus more as needed
ingredients.prep: for the pan, plus more as needed

steps: Cut the pork into long strips or chunks 2 to 3 inches thick. Leave the fat on; it renders and adds flavor.
In a bowl, combine the sugar, salt, five spice, white pepper, sesame oil, wine, soy sauce, hoisin, molasses, food coloring (if using), and garlic to make the marinade.
Reserve about 2 tbsp of the marinade, covered, in the refrigerator. Rub the pork with the rest in a large bowl or baking dish, cover, and refrigerate overnight or at least 8 hours.
Position a rack in the upper third of the oven and preheat to 475°F (bake setting). A convection oven will roast faster, so check often.

Line a sheet pan with foil and set a metal rack on top. Lay the pork on the rack with as much space between pieces as possible, and pour the 1 1/2 cups water into the pan below to keep the drippings from burning.

Roast for 10 minutes at 475°F, then lower the oven to 375°F and roast 15 minutes more (25 minutes total). Flip the pork, add another cup of water if the pan is dry, and turn the pan 180 degrees. Roast 15 minutes more. Check every 10 minutes and lower the heat if the edges start to burn.
Meanwhile, stir the reserved marinade with the maltose or honey and the 1 tbsp hot water to make a basting sauce (warm maltose in the microwave to loosen it).

After 40 minutes of roasting, baste the pork, flip it, and baste the other side. Roast a final 10 minutes, until caramelized and the center reads at least 145°F. For more char, broil for 1-2 minutes, watching closely.
Baste with the last of the sauce and rest the pork for 10 minutes before slicing.
tips: Oven temperatures vary; an oven thermometer helps, and so does checking the pork every 10 minutes during the roast.
